title: S205--Solicitation Marion National Cemetery Trash Services
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF > NATIONAL CEMETERY ADMIN (36C786)
description:
Site Access
I was hoping you could provide clarity regarding site access. Will a contractor/subcontractor require any kind of badge/permit to gain access to the site and the locations of the dumpsters in addition to regular permits and licenses required for regular operation?
A: No badge/ permit is required for the site. The location of the dumpsters is illustrated on page 14 of the solicitation. Technical requirements for submission are listed on page 34.

Quantity
I want to make sure I m reading the posting correctly. From what I understand you are requesting
12 months x one 6-yard general waste containers emptied weekly
12 months x one 20-yard general waste/headstone/construction materials container emptied monthly with 2 tons monthly included.

Estimated annual overage fee for on-call general waste/headstone/construction material containers not expected to exceed 10 tons per year

We are performing independent research on the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (36C78627Q0019). We would like to know if this is a brand-new contract OR if there is (was) an incumbent performing these services. If not brand new, could you please provide the current / previous contract number and what the total contract value was?

A: This is a new requirementÂ 

CLIN 0001 is priced per month for a "6-yard General waste container emptied weekly," while SOW A.1.1 refers to "the required size and quantity of containers." How many 6-yard containers are required, and are they front-load containers with lids?
A: 1 6 yard container.

CLIN 0002 describes the 20-yard container as "emptied monthly" (12 EA), while SOW A.1.2 describes on-call, as-needed delivery and pickup within 3 business days. Should offerors price 12 on-call 20-yard hauls per year, and is the 20-yard container kept on site between hauls or delivered only when called?
A: the 20 yard container will remain on site and be emptied monthly.

Can the Government provide historical tonnage for the 20-yard container (last 12 24 months of weight tickets, total tons and average tons per pull) to support the 2-ton allowance and the 10-ton estimated annual overage?
A: Past weight tickets are not available.

Is there a Government-recommended landfill or disposal facility for this contract, and are there any special handling requirements for disposing of headstones (e.g., must headstones be broken, defaced or recycled rather than landfilled)?
A: The government request is for waste removal services. Disposal of wastes is contractors decision. Headstones will be broken prior to placement in the dumpster. 

Are concrete landing pads already in place at the 6-yard and 20-yard container locations shown on the site map, and are there any weight limits on cemetery roads for roll-off trucks?
A: No. The 6 yard will be in a gravel lot. The 20 yard will go in the spoils lot which is a mix of gravel/dirt.

SF1449 Block 8 lists the quote due date as 12-04-2026 at 16:00 EDT, while the SAM.gov notice lists 11:00 AM EST. Which date/time and time zone governs?
A: The latest time governs.

We would manage the contract and a licensed Indiana hauler would perform the work as our named subcontractor. Will the subcontractor's FMCSA DOT registration and IDEM registration meet the technical requirement?
Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance.

Will past performance references from the named subcontractor be accepted?
Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance.

The RFQ refers to an "IDEM license." Which IDEM registration or permit number should the quote show for a solid waste hauler?
A: License to provide services in accordance with: https://www.in.gov/idem/waste/resources/permits-registrations-approvals-and-closures/

Does VAAR 852.219-75 apply, given that the RFQ is unrestricted?
852.219-75 does not apply, however the technical factor of the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance does apply.

How many 6-yard containers are required? The CLIN says "container" and the SOW says "containers at each active site."
A: 1 container

Could you share the current contract number for this service?
A: No current contract

Technical acceptability (Volume B). Section E.3 (FAR 52.212-2) establishes award on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable basis, with Technical Acceptability as a pass/fail factor, but the solicitation does not list the elements that make a quotation technically acceptable. Could you confirm the specific minimum requirements the Government will evaluate, and whether a Volume B technical response is required in addition to the Volume A administrative documents described in the Instructions to Quoters?
A: Technical acceptability is listed on page 34.
